1. Client cài trên VPS là **snx-rs6.5.1**, dự án cộng đồng, **không phải client
   CheckPoint chính thức**. Người dùng báo client Windows của họ vẫn kết nối tốt,
   phiên24giờ; đây là thông tin người dùng cung cấp, không được phủ nhận bằng logLinux.
2. PhiênLinux đầu kết nối được khoảng12:17UTC, đã SSH/chạy PBS/download thành công.
   Log cuối chính xác20:17:01UTC: `IKE SA expired, disconnecting tunnel`, sau đó
   `Tunnel disconnected`, exit0. Không phải bằng chứng server/VPNWindows hết phiên.
3. Đã đọc đúng sourcev6.5.1, revision
   `86aa48031888050f957af7b6adf2c2e39d4745fd`: mặc định
   **ike-lifetime28800giây=8giờ**, helper cũ không override. Client đề xuất giá trị
   này khi tạo SA, dùng lifetime đã đàm phán để tự ngắt khi hết hạn. Đây là điểm
   cấu hình bỏ sót phù hợp thời điểm ngắt; không phải kết luận server chỉ cho8giờ.
4. Helper hiện đã sửa **`--ike-lifetime86400` (24giờ)** cho kết nối IPsec mới.
   Gateway vẫn có thể áp lifetime riêng; **chưa thử thành công phiên mới với
   cấu hình này, chưa chứng minh giữ được24giờ**.
5. Đã thử login lại hai lần được ghi nhận,20:40 và20:47UTC: gateway trả
   `IPsec authentication failed,status0` / `Authentication failed`. Đây là
   **lỗi xác thực VPN**, xảy ra trước SSH. Chưa xác định do mật khẩu, DUO, chính
   sách hay nguyên nhân khác. Không tự kết luận mật khẩu sai hoặc hết phiên.
   Lần20:47 bắt đầu trước khi helper được sửa; không tính là phép thử24giờ.
6. Câu hỏi DUO đã gửi người dùng: điện thoại đội trưởng có yêu cầu khớp lần login
   hay không. Chưa có câu trả lời tại mốc ghi này. Không tự phê duyệt DUO.
7. **ControlPersist86400 là SSH**, không phải VPN lifetime.
   **ike-persist là lưu/khôi phục SA lên đĩa**, không đồng nghĩa tự rekey.
8. VPN mất không tự hủy job PBS đã nhận. Chưa kết nối được thì chưa biết trạng
   thái/kết quả cuối của job; không gửi job thay thế trùng lặp.

# Startup counters prepared 2026-10-15 20:20 UTC

`startup-sampler.py` is a local, unsubmitted diagnostic companion. It does not
change the frozen baseline or pilots04/05/06, stage assets, reserve SU or start
a GPU job. It imports only the Python standard library. Runtime on NSCC is
unverified because the existing VPN helper no longer finds a live session and
the existing SSH master timed out on a read-only query in this wake.

For a future instrumented allocation, launch one sampler per worker **inside
its compute container**, immediately before its final `exec` of SGLang. Supply
that worker shell's PID as `--root-pid` and a fresh artifact JSONL path as
`--out`; defaults are15s intervals and a1200s maximum. Keep the sampler's
`PBS_JOBID` in the container explicitly (the current cleanenv wrapper only
forwards QWEN variables). Run the identical observation policy for matched
control and candidate allocations before interpreting a difference. Any such
bundle must be frozen/validated separately; these instructions do not authorize
an additional simultaneous job or bypass queue, quality or budget gates.

The sampler checks UID and PID start time, walks children from the explicit
root's per-thread child lists, and excludes its own subtree. It reads only
stat/status/io/numa_maps for that tree. Output contains CPU ticks, thread count,
minor/major faults, RSS, I/O counters, CPU/memory affinity and aggregated NUMA
page counts; it never records command lines, environments or mapped filenames.
It refuses to overwrite prior evidence and its CLI requires a PBS allocation.

Interpretation:

- Use counter deltas only for the same PID/start-time identity. A newly seen
  process has no delta; exited children are missing, so sums undercount work.
- Divide CPU-tick deltas by clock ticks and elapsed sample time to estimate
  CPU use. Compare thread count and CPU masks against the allocated32CPUs per
  TP4 replica; do not infer actual NUMA locality from a CPU mask alone.
- Correlate major faults/read_bytes and NUMA placement with shard progress and
  `/get_server_info` startup times. mmap faults, shared page cache, readahead and
  network filesystem accounting prevent equating read_bytes with model traffic.
- RSS/NUMA pages can count shared mappings repeatedly across ranks. Do not sum
  RSS as physical node memory or interpret node page totals as per-GPU distance.
- Stable low I/O with high CPU suggests a different next investigation from
  high fault/I/O stalls, but neither proves causality. Storage/cache state and
  TP/EP topology must stay explicit. Do not flush system caches.

The real image source additionally shows that expert locality is checked in
`fused_moe_triton/layer.py:927–938` **after** the iterator hands a tensor to
`qwen3_moe.py:1125–1200`. The default mmap iterator builds dictionaries of
`get_tensor` views before the expert loader may skip a nonlocal weight.
This establishes control-flow order; it does not establish whether those
skipped tensors' data pages were read or an eightfold I/O reduction. Therefore
the851s versus99s prefill/decode load times remain confounded observations.

Local validation uses a controlled own child writing4MiB and spawning an own
grandchild; it checks descendant discovery, identity, counters and CLI refusal
outside PBS. No model imports or GPU execution are involved. Evidence is in
`inspection/wake-20261015-2020UTC/startup-sampler-validation.json`.

## Offline analysis prepared 2026-10-15 20:57 UTC

`python3 analyze-startup.py WORKER.jsonl --out FRESH-analysis.json` reads one
sampler journal without accessing processes, model files or GPUs. Run separately
for each worker. It uses monotonic sample times and metadata clock ticks to
calculate observed CPU-seconds/wall-second and I/O rates. It recomputes deltas
from raw counters for matching `(pid,start_ticks)` identities rather than trusting
embedded deltas. New/disappeared identities, missing counter coverage, resets,
read errors and gaps over1.5times the nominal interval remain explicit.
Missing coverage produces null, not zero. CPU cores do not represent a percent
of allocated CPUs. No summed RSS, storage-throughput claim or automatic
bottleneck classification is produced.

An unfinished final JSONL line is ignored and flagged for live snapshots;
malformed complete lines and nonincreasing monotonic times are rejected.
Output uses exclusive creation and retains the input SHA256. Keep the original
journal. A single sample has no rate interval and is not evidence of inactivity.

Offline validation passed PID reuse, missing I/O, counter reset, sample gap,
incomplete tail, invalid inputs and refusal to overwrite. Previously preserved
local own-child samples reproduce wchar4194309 and write_bytes0. Their analysis
has explicitly constructed local-test metadata; it is not a NSCC measurement.
Evidence: `inspection/wake-20261015-2055UTC/analyzer-validation.json`.
Sampler and analyzer remain local only; frozen04/05/06 and their priority,
queue/budget gates are unchanged. No instrumentation has run on NSCC.

# Profile-guided decode experiments

Updated 2026-10-15. All scripts and submission notes are in English. Qwen track only.

## Measured position

Round-robin N52 now has three independent measurements: 2402.64 (23325),
2397.72 (23576), and 2400.02 (23607) good output tokens/s, each approximately
98.93% SLA. N53 reached **2433.41 good tokens/s, 98.88% SLA** (23616), the highest
observed passing N53 point at that time. Its independent repeat **23773** completed
at **2438.47 good tokens/s, 98.88% SLA**, with zero errors/cancellations. The N53
gain is now reproduced at this topology. N54 passed SLA but fell to2358.64.

The round-robin backend experiments completed, with zero errors/cancellations:

| Job | Backend change | Good tokens/s | SLA | Decision |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 23608 | FP8 E4M3 KV on both roles | 254.47 | 10.75% | Reject at N52: mean ITL20.069ms crosses the20ms gate |
| 23609 | Decode DeepGEMM MoE | 2021.39 | 84.71% | Reject at N52: below90% SLA |

These are completed measurements that **failed the latency requirement**.
Their raw output rates were2368.03 and2386.12 tokens/s respectively; raw speed
does not compensate for request latency failures. Neither triggered an automatic
repeat or a higher-load job. Eight-case output diagnostics matched the known
baseline failure pattern; organiser full-set accuracy remains unverified.

## New evidence and hypotheses

Job23607 captured all16 GPU rank traces after its official benchmark, using
separate52-request diagnostic traffic. The retained summary is
[kernel-summary.json](../runs/23607/diagnostic-profile/kernel-summary.json).
Representative decode TP0 summed GPU kernel durations included27.40% MoE,
20.06% collectives, and19.64% in the main BF16 FA3 attention kernel.
These fractions are **not wall-clock shares or predicted speedups**.

Three independent N52 tests use the frozen round-robin bundle from23576:

| Job | Trial | Only change |
|---|---|---|
| 23776 | CUTLASS MoE | Decode `--moe-runner-backend cutlass` |
| 23777 | FlashInfer attention | Decode `--decode-attention-backend flashinfer` |
| 23778 | MNNVL collective | Decode `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend mnnvl` |

CUTLASS targets the grouped block-FP8 expert GEMMs. The actual staged source
has an SM90 path for this quantization, separate from its SM100-only MXFP8 path.
FlashInfer targets the decode attention work while keeping prefill FA3, BF16 KV,
page size and NIXL geometry unchanged. The staged collective resolver explicitly
allows MNNVL on SM90 within one node; decode TP8 is entirely on one node even
though the full P/D deployment occupies two nodes. This compares an alternative
fused allreduce implementation with the profiled TRTLLM path.

The exact staged source snapshots and hashes are in [inspection](inspection/).
These are compatibility checks from source; successful GPU startup and the
effective backend still need checking in each run's logs. A backend that silently
falls back must be reported as such before attributing a gain to its kernel.

All tests retain16 H200, P8-TP4_D8-TP8-EP8, BF16 KV, all model experts, official
FP8 checkpoint, chunk4096, dense decode graphs1–64, round-robin prefill routing,
request-scoped NIXL patch, and the unmodified benchmark/client. No below-FP8
format or quantized communication is enabled. Every scored point uses
60s warmup /120s measurement /30s grace,4000 input /200 output tokens.

## Queue and decision policy

The original N53 repeat keeps its queue position. The initial controller limit
was four pending/running jobs. On2026-10-15, public Slurm QoS inspection confirmed
the actual per-user pending/running limit is five; active wave7 plans were amended
to five, sharing that cap with the new DP-attention pilot23780. The45-second
controller keeps progressing without another user prompt.

For each measured backend, require a full passing N52 point with no errors or
cancellations and the same-attempt output research gate. A gain of at least2%
over both the original N52 reference and the fresh23607 N52 control triggers
one independent N52 repeat. Only a repeat that preserves that gain, SLA≥95%
and mean ITL≤19.3ms triggers N54. This bounded wave permits at most nine
deployments: three initial tests and up to two dependent tests per candidate,
apart from explicitly recorded budget retries. Failures without exports remain
incomplete, and never count as a measured load boundary.

The current N53 best must also be beaten before selecting a new performance
winner. Full organiser accuracy is required before contest promotion; a fast
benchmark or an eight-case smoke diagnostic cannot establish the99% gate.
The submission package is not automatically replaced by experimental results.
